This is your father's mother's line: Glenda Kirkland, Buster Kirkland and Joy Moss, and every line above them (Kirkland, Moss, Culberson, Tippens, Williams, Giles, Davis, Bryant, Martin, Bivens, Turner, Pulliam, Stone).
tasks.unlocks: The tree gains every generation the records support, each link with an honest percentage; the false links online are named so nobody adds them.
inputs: The seed, read first: https://jpavia10.github.io/prometheus-hub/pillars/kin/lineage/data.js (every person, source, conflict, the certainty of each link in L.certainty, the research log). The method: https://github.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/blob/main/pillars/kin/docs/LINEAGE_METHOD.md. The tree to see it: https://jpavia10.github.io/prometheus-hub/pillars/kin/tree/.

Your Ancestry.com trial on Joseph's 'Pavia Family Tree' (tree 192482486), signed in as before; FamilySearch (free account); the NARA 1950 census site (1950census.archives.gov); Find a Grave; Michiganology; WikiTree; Newspapers.com clippings that members have shared.

The people to start from: P-glenda, P-buster, P-joy, P-jessec, P-juliaw, P-chester, P-ada and every id above them. The certainty each link has now: L.certainty in the seed (Claude's figure; your earlier figure as 'gemini' where Claude set it lower).
steps: For every person on the line, from the youngest up: their parents, with the certainty of the link on the scale and the records behind it by name (census year and county, will, marriage, death certificate, obituary).
Keep going up each branch until no record supports a further link; then one more row: the best candidate parents and why they are under 40%.
List every link you meet online that is wrong (kind disproved): who claims it, where, and the record that disproves it.
Never give 90 or more to a link that rests on compiled trees or indexes alone; a primary record must name the parent.
Last row: kind summary: the deepest generation reached on each branch, how many links at each band, and the records that would raise the weakest five.

deliver.shape: JSON array, one object per row, exactly the fields below; the last row is kind 'summary'

fields.name: kind
fields.rule: link (one parent-to-child link), disproved (a link seen online that is wrong), or summary

fields.name: child
fields.rule: data.js id (P-...) or NEW-<given>-<surname>-<birth year>

fields.name: child_name
fields.rule: full name, birth-death years

fields.name: parent
fields.rule: id or NEW-...

fields.name: parent_name
fields.rule: full name, birth-death years

fields.name: role
fields.rule: father or mother

fields.name: certainty
fields.rule: the scale: 90-100 a primary record names the parent; 70-89 indexes and consensus agree; 40-69 working hypothesis; under 40 disputed or disproved

fields.name: basis
fields.rule: the records behind the figure, by name and date (not 'FamilySearch')

fields.name: urls
fields.rule: every record page used, separated by ' | '

fields.name: against
fields.rule: anything that argues against the link, or 'nothing found'

tasks.done_when: Every branch of the line followed to its last supported generation, every link scored with its records, the false online links listed.
checks: Claude checks the records of fifteen links at random against their percentage.
Claude rejects the file if any 90+ link rests on trees or indexes alone.
rejected_if: a record presented as the person's without at least three identifiers compared
a transcription shortened, paraphrased or 'cleaned'
a hint accepted or a tree edit made without the identity argument
a percentage without the records that justify it
a portrait used as someone's likeness without saying who labelled it and why it is them
addresses of living people, phone numbers or people-search sites (Whitepages, FastBackgroundCheck): leave them out
searches that found nothing left out
